primitives.name: Falsifier Verdict Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: --description: Run a bind through the falsifier and record the verdict.
primitives.assumptions: Edge must pass four kill tests; sample size n ≥ minN; model probability ≠ confidence/100
primitives.breakdown_regime: When n < minN → STARVED; when edge fails one test → KILLED

layer2.mapping: Verdicts map to Bayesian posterior updates in GSI; GSE transitions between belief states using these outcomes as telemetry.

primitives.name: Acceptance Harness Validator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Confirm the acceptance harness is green — planted edge + pure noise + inverted, at n ∈ {100, 1k, 5k}.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'Harness status {green, red}', 'n': 'sample size ∈ {100, 1000, 5000}', 'E': 'Planted edge signal', 'N': 'Pure noise component'}
primitives.assumptions: Harness must validate edge signal integrity across multiple scales
primitives.breakdown_regime: If harness fails validation, no further falsification is permitted

layer2.mapping: Harness ensures data consistency before applying falsifier logic; acts as pre-conditioner for GSI's probabilistic inference engine.
layer2.telemetry: Green/red flag from synthetic edge+noise evaluation

primitives.name: Kill Test Sequence
primitives.verbatim_quote: Record the verdict verbatim, with e-values: - `SURVIVOR` — passed all four kill tests - `KILLED` — failed one.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_i': 'i-th kill test {0,1}', 'E_i': 'e-value for test i', 'K': 'number of failed tests'}
primitives.assumptions: Each test independently evaluates edge resilience; K=0 implies SURVIVOR
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure of any single test results in KILLED classification

layer2.mapping: Sequence of binary kill tests mirrors GSI's sequential hypothesis rejection process; GSE uses outcome to update internal state models.
layer2.telemetry: Binary pass/fail flags per test, aggregated into final verdict

The falsifier operates as a structured empirical risk minimizer, where each bind undergoes a sequence of kill tests to assess its robustness. The verdicts (SURVIVOR/KILLED/STARVED/PARKED) represent conditional probabilities under varying sample sizes and model assumptions. The acceptance harness ensures that only valid signals proceed, acting as a filter for downstream inference. The kill test sequence enforces a binary decision tree, mirroring Bayesian hypothesis testing. Each test contributes an e-value, which quantifies the strength of evidence against the null hypothesis. When n < minN, the edge is STARVED due to insufficient data; when one test fails, it is KILLED. These classifications form a lattice of logical dependencies, enabling GSI to compute posterior distributions and GSE to transition between belief states.
